en: Mangrove trees in coastal swamps grow specialized upward-pointing roots called pneumatophores to breathe air during high tide.
Male fiddler crabs in muddy coastal areas have one claw significantly larger than the other to attract mates.
The human stomach produces strong hydrochloric acid to break down food and kill harmful bacteria during digestion.
The mosquito life cycle includes four distinct stages: egg, larva, pupa, and adult, with the first three living in water.
Coral reefs in the Coral Triangle support high biodiversity by providing shelter and food for thousands of marine fish species.
The Asian water monitor lizard uses its powerful tail to swim efficiently and its sharp claws to climb trees.
Dengue fever is a viral illness transmitted to humans through the bite of an infected female Aedes aegypti mosquito.
Rice plants survive in flooded paddies because their stems contain hollow tissues that transport oxygen directly down to their roots.
The carabao cools its body by wallowing in mud because it lacks sufficient sweat glands to regulate its temperature.
The dense canopy of the tropical rainforest blocks sunlight from reaching the forest floor, limiting the growth of ground-level plants.
The golden kuhol lays bright pink egg clusters on dry surfaces above the water to protect them from aquatic predators.
The makahiya plant quickly folds its leaves when touched to protect itself from hungry herbivores and harsh physical damage.
